daily_rhythm.about: When the van brings you and takes you away (issue 198, DailyRhythm). Never a workday: arrival is the first sign of the day; departure is evening quiet (hours with no turn, once it is dusk), a long evening lock or sleep (minutes), or night. The wrap-up time (a setting, off by default) invites once: within wrap_grace_min of it; then quiet for wrap_quiet_min leaves, still busy after wrap_decide_min stays. The start-of-day time (a setting, off by default; issue 431): after it the van comes only when you are at this Mac, unlocked with the last keyboard or mouse input within present_within_sec (the native extension's idle seconds, nothing else); start_default is the time the switch offers. poll_sec: how often the Mac's signals are read.

welcome.about: The first-run welcome (issue 199): opens by itself once, when you have stepped out of the van; the field kit's look, Config's size. python is where the connect step looks for a Python 3.11+ to run game/tools/hook_install.py (first that exists; VIBENATURE_PYTHON wins). night_open_sec: with no van at night, how long after launch it opens.

demo_card.about: The demo's morning card (issue 268): once a game day, when the van brings you in, a field-kit note over the scene says this is the demo and offers more places. The demo build only (Edition, issue 247). show_sec in all, faded in over fade_in_sec and out over the last fade_out_sec; its centre at x_share of the window width, inset_pt from the top (over the sky, clear of the log, the van and the strip); url is a placeholder until the site exists (issue 248).
demo_card.heading: This is the VibeNature demo
demo_card.body: The pond is yours to keep, free. More than twenty other quiet places are waiting whenever you'd like them.

letter_card.about: The elder's letter on the scene while you read it on the log (issue 314): a field-kit note card gap_pt to the right of you, inset_pt from the window's top, width_pt wide. Fades in over fade_in_sec as you unfold it and out over fade_out_sec as you fold it; a click or Esc closes it over close_sec. In a window under full_min_height_pt tall (50%), or one the whole letter does not fit, the first small_lines lines and the button; the portrait is left out there when taller than small_portrait_max_pt.

avatar_looks.about: The avatar is one of the bench's ten looks (assets/avatar/looks, Skypatch issue 202) with skin, hair and top colours swapped in. from_old maps the six old whole avatars to the nearest look and skin (skin measured on their faces); island_avatar is the old whole avatar the island game wears per body. silhouette is the look each Body tile's silhouette is cut from. Picker crops are in sheet px round the anchor: [x, y, w, h].

elder.about: The elder's letters (issue 213; proposal 2026-10-18-the-elder-2.md section 4). Decided once a game day while you are not at the log (overnight); at most one waits. Letters, elders and the never-list are in data/elder/. Days are game days.

day.about: The van and you coming and going (issues 198, 255). The van is the bench's sheet (`van.art` + `van.meta`, issue 197; files of the companion package, `SceneVan.file`), drawn at the far band 1:1 with its anchor on `route.lane_y_pt`; a missing file draws nothing. Arriving it cruises in from the right, facing left, from behind the oak (`from_x_pt`, hidden there; issue 279) and brakes evenly over `brake_m` to `park_x_pt` (about mid-bank, parked facing left); leaving it makes a three-point turn (`turn`) and pulls away over `pull_away_m` to the right, on behind the oak (`to_x_pt`, hidden). A stop settles the body `settle_px` for `settle_sec`. Its wheels turn by distance: one drive cycle per `wheel_m_per_cycle`. You walk at `route.walk_m_per_sec` (the walk's frames by the ground covered): out of the van's door along the far bank to `far_hide_x_pt` (wholly behind the near bank's plants), `hidden_sec` out of sight, then in from `near_from_x_pt` (off the scene's left edge) to the log. All in points. A look without day art fades at the log over `fade_sec`. The van's lamps (issue 277) are on for any departure or arrival from `lamps.from` until `lamps.until` (each [day phase, minutes after its start]: dusk until sunrise), and for leaving after the wrap-up whenever it is.

glow.about: The van's lamps glowing (issue 279): a light effect in code (additive radial sprites), never drawn art. Lamps are found in the bench's lit frames (pixels that differ from the unlit twin, in blobs of at most lamp_max_px below lamp_min_y_share of the frame, bright (head_min_value) or strong red (tail_min_saturation)). darkness 0..1 from the light's tint luminance between lum_day (none) and lum_dark (full) scales both the glow round each lamp (radius_px art px, tail lamps tail_share of it, at strength) and the pool on the ground ahead (pool_px [w, h] radii, pool_ahead_px beyond the headlamps; front-on, pool_front_dy_px nearer the viewer; at pool_strength).

turn.about: The evening's three-point turn (issue 279): forward toward the viewer forward_m (and toward_viewer_m nearer), a stop of hold_sec with the lamps on the viewer, reverse reverse_m over turn_forward's first reverse_frames views, a stop of stop_sec, then forward out_m out of the turn from rest into the pull-away. Metres along the bank.

shelter.about: Sheltering in the van from the rain (issue 476, SceneShelter, SceneVan.shelter): you go as the first drops show (the human, PR 484): the rain at go_rain or more (just over SceneRain.VISIBLE, where drops start) for go_sec, a fraction of a second, walking the evening's route without the stretch hurry times as fast (the day actions too) with hidden_sec out of sight; you come back once it has stayed under back_rain (no drops drawn) for back_sec, at the route's own pace. Inside, the bench's lit window pixels (warm: red at least window_min_red, blue at most window_max_blue, in blobs of window_min_px or more, above the lamps) show over the parked van, fading in and out over light_sec, lit window_keep of the way from the light's tint to white, and an additive glow (glow_colour) of glow_scale times each window's size at glow_day by day plus glow_dark times the darkness.

far_tree.about: Far-band trees (kind far_tree, Skypatch issue 165), in points: reach_pt is the top's lean per unit of wind past the calm band (pushed by (wind - calm_wind)^curve), max_pt caps it; response_spread varies each tree's frequency and damping so a gust rolls across tree by tree; shimmer is the share of a broadleaf crown's texels lit in a strong gust.

letter.about: Reading the elder's letter on the log (issue 270), once per letter at the end of the first rest after you settle: out, open, read, look up at the water for look_up_sec, back down, read again, put away. His whole reading (and so the letter card on the scene, issue 317) lasts as long as the letter needs: its words / words_per_sec + extra_sec, clamped to read_total_sec; the look up is inside that, and read_share of the rest is the first read.

glance_down.about: A glance down at his hands and lap (the looking-down heads, issue 313), held hold_sec, then back up.

breath.about: Visible breathing for whole-sprite looks (issue 123): on the in-breath (the in_share part of each breath) the rows above_hip_px above the hips (the log anchor) are drawn lift_px art px higher in the seated shader; the legs and the hands on the knees stay put. Each breath takes a random sec (doze_sec asleep).

watch.about: Watching animals (issue 123): something in sight draws his eyes while he rests or glances, for far_sec (one close by, near_pt: up to near_max_sec, and watched at once when it comes), then he lets it be for gap_sec. The way he looks changes only after min_dir_sec; out of sight for under lose_sec he keeps looking where it was. Close, more than below_pt below the hips and within down_reach_pt to the side: he looks down at it (within down_mid_pt: straight down; once down, down_give_pt looser). Reading, his eyes come up from the page after page_min_sec for far_sec x from_book_share.

chill.about: How cold it feels at the log, 0..1 (the thermos's weight): each share times mist, wind mean, cloud, rain and the dark.

activities.about: Activities with their own sheets (issue 123), each in -> loop -> out; a look without the sheet skips it. weight x the hours curve ([minute of day, factor], straight between) x (1 + chill x how cold) x the rain's share toward rain. thermos: picked up from the ground (out of the bag the first time), sips, then stood on the ground again (set_down_share the first time), where it stays until he packs up. paperback: read_sec in pages of page_sec, a page turned or (look_up_chance) a look out at the water between; never below dark_below daylight. fidget: the look's fidget sheet (issue 321) once delivered, weight shared between its fidgets, each held hold_sec.

drowsy.about: Drowsy but awake, on a seat that does not support dozing (issue 121): weight_night times the dark (1 - daylight); one beat of a slow stretch, a long look up, or the chin dipping for dip_sec and caught with a look up for catch_sec.

variation.about: Natural variation (issue 272): each animal's own pace, a share either side of its kind's (walking, swimming, wingbeat and tail-beat), and how far (points) an arrival's first stop keeps from the last few of its kind (the director's `place_memory`). A species may override either in its own `variation`.

depth_views.about: Which way a bird or fish is seen from its heading (issue 237): degrees off the picture plane where three-quarter starts and straight toward/away starts, the margin past a line before the view changes, the least time between changes, how long the heading is smoothed, the slowest way that still counts (m/s), how long the old view dissolves under the new, and how long a step to the next crisp size dissolves (a heron flying into the scene)

on_oak.about: An animal on or against the oak (issue 343, 351) is drawn near true size against it: the oak's band scale (mid, 140 art px/m: the trunk is 143 art px, 1.02 m, across at the squirrel's height) times show_scale, and the sheet set and whole scale nearest that (SceneBehaviour.on_oak_ppm_art). Larger than life there makes the oak read small. blend_m: metres from the perch over which a hawk coming in goes from its pass size to this.

grass.about: The grass behind the right bank's shore strip (issue 237): a mid-bank animal sometimes comes out of the reeds instead of in from the edge (come_out_chance), sometimes goes into them when it leaves calmly (go_in_chance), and bounds into them away from a threat when the edge lies toward it (threat_side_pt: how far to its left the threat may be and still count as toward the edge). In the grass it is drawn in actor layer `layer`, behind the reeds: it stands there `hidden_sec` (fading in first over `fade_sec`), never longer than `max_hidden_sec` in all, then steps out onto the open strip. Going in it fades over `fade_sec` (`flee_fade_sec` running), walking on into the stand at `into_m_per_sec`.

depth_run.about: a fish drawn from the front and behind sometimes swims into the depth or out of it toward the glass instead of across (issue 237): the chance per cruise, the least change of depth, its speed as a share of its swim, and degrees off straight in or out

depth.about: fish in depth, front glass 0 to back murk 1 (Skypatch issue 156): drawn size at the back (a crisp set picks it: @back, or the master at 1/2), haze and dimming at the back, how fast a fish drifts in depth (share per second; leave_rate times that going), the actor layer by depth (behind the near weeds when back), a school's spread, metres front to back for fears, the crossfade between crisp sizes, the nose-down pitch of a dive, and how fast a fish further back fades going up into the light under the surface before it clears the water out on the pond at the row for its depth (leap_fade_sec, issue 237)

sitter_morning.about: issue 123: a quiet morning on the log: breathing, a drink from the thermos stood back on the ground, songbirds dropping to the grass by his feet (he looks down at them), and his idle life after

sitter_reading.about: issue 123: reading the paperback at midday, the thermos on the ground beside the log

sitter_night.about: issue 121: the log late at night: drowsy but awake (a slow stretch, a long look up, the chin dipping and caught), never asleep

screencast.about: issue 475: the website's screencasts; `just screencast` records a real Claude Code session and plays its hook events here (VIBENATURE_CLIP_TIMELINE); these events are a sample of one

letter_morning.about: issue 270: the morning with a letter due: arrive, sit, take the letter out, read, look up at the water, put it away

depth_views.about: issue 237 part 1: fish swimming into the depth (seen from behind) and out toward the glass (from the front), turning through three-quarter, and the heron gliding in, then flying away over the pond into the scene

shore.about: issue 237: the right bank's shore in use (the heron hunting on the wet edge, a deer on the strip) and a bluegill at the back rising and leaping out on the pond

deer_drink.about: issue 320: a doe and her fawn come down to drink on the right bank's strip; one keeps watch while the other drinks

glide_left.about: issue 272: a glide-in high from the left (cut together with glide_far and glide_above)

speed_limits.about: issue 318: a songbird party landing and flitting, a heron gliding in out of the distance, a few songbirds coming and going, all at real speeds

glide_far.about: issue 272: a glide-in out of the distance over the far treeline

glide_above.about: issue 272: a glide-in dropping in from over the top of the picture

glide_low.about: issue 272: a glide-in low over the treetops from the left

geese_landing.about: issue 356: a line of Canada geese comes in over the far trees, swings round and lands on the water one after another; they settle, swim, dabble, preen, one stretches; then a running takeoff (stay pinned short for the clip)

wood_ducks.about: issue 378: a pair of wood ducks comes in fast and splashes down on the open water, settles, swims, dabbles and preens (the seed picks the side, the spot and the rest; nothing pinned)

wood_ducks_flush.about: issue 378: the pair splashes down, a short stay, then they flush off the water and leave fast (pinned: from the left, the flush; stills of each beat)

wood_duck_brood.about: issue 378: late spring, a wood duck hen leads her ducklings out from behind the near bank, stops while they bunch round her, and leads them back (pinned: the brood, seven ducklings)

wood_ducks_off.about: issue 378: the pair splashes down from the right, a short stay, then they swim off one after the other behind the near bank (pinned; stills)

turtles.about: issue 370: painted turtles basking on the snag in the near water slide off one after another, plop, plop, plop, and dive away through the cut-away; after a quiet spell heads pop up one at a time out on the near water, one paddles, and they come back under water and climb out one by one (the seed picks how many, the order and the rest; nothing pinned). 158 s played, the quiet stretches cut (skip): 45 s

osprey_dive.about: issue 362: an osprey comes in high over the far trees, circles, hovers over the open water, stoops and plunges feet first, sits in the water, labours up with a fish, shakes off in mid-air and carries it off over the trees (outcome pinned to a catch for the clip; the seed picks the rest)

kingfisher_hover.about: issue 364: the kingfisher's other way of fishing, pinned: out from the twig to a hover over the near water, the plunge, back with a fish (stills of its beats)

kingfisher.about: issue 364: a belted kingfisher in low along the water, up onto a bare twig of the oak's long limb, bobs, dives head first (the seed picks drop or hover), a splash and rings, back with a fish, beats it on the branch, swallows it, sits, then rattles off along the water

beaver.about: issue 366: at dusk a beaver swims across the open water between the log and the reeds, startled it slaps its tail with a burst of spray and dives, surfaces farther off and watches, then swims on out behind the near bank or sinks by the reeds (the slap pinned; the seed picks the rest)

beaver_cross.about: issue 366: at dawn a beaver carries a leafy branch across the open water, its wake spreading behind it (pinned: the crossing; stills)

otters.about: issue 368: a family of river otters porpoising across the open pond in a line, then playing in one place (the seed picks the rest; nothing pinned)

otters_bank.about: issue 368: otters porpoising in while one lopes along the shore strip and slides off the point's tip into the water; a catch carried to the bank and eaten there (pinned: slide and bank; stills of each beat)

deer_bound.about: issue 372: the deer moment on a hand-off with nothing pinned: deer bound in out of cover, land and stand alert, white tails up, then drink with one on watch (the seed picks the strip or the meadow, the group and the way in)

deer_startle.about: issue 372: a doe drinking at the shore strip startles (head up, ears forward, a stamp) and bounds off with her tail flagging; a while later she comes back cautiously to the edge and looks (pinned: startle on the strip; stills of each beat)

deer_meadow.about: issue 372: a doe and her fawns drinking at the far waterline startle and bound off into the treeline, flags up; one comes back out, looks, then the others (pinned: startle on the meadow)

swallows.about: issue 374: a loose group of tree swallows streaks in low over the water, hawks over the pond banking, twisting and dipping to drink, then leaves together (the seed picks everything; nothing pinned)

swallows_perch.about: issue 374: eight tree swallows in from the right, every beat early (a twist, a glide, a swoop, a dip, a wingover), three sitting in a row on the oak's bare limb, leaving to the left (pinned; stills of each beat)

hatch.about: issue 376: a warm calm June evening, the mayfly hatch: duns popping up across the near water and rings breaking out everywhere, sunfish and a bass rising through the cut-away, the males dancing over the water, spinners falling spent, then the rises thinning and the last duns fluttering away (the seed picks it all; nothing pinned)

hatch_leap.about: issue 376: the hatch with a bass breaking clear after a mayfly (pinned: the leap; stills of each beat)

sun_cloud.about: issue 380: clouds crossing the low afternoon sun (they pass in front of it; the clouds at six times their speed)

sun_glow.about: issue 472: clouds crossing the afternoon sun at eight times their speed: a faint glow through their thin edges, the rim bright beside it, the thick body hiding the disc (stills)

sun_glow_sunset.about: issue 472: the same at sunset, the low sun's orange through a thin edge (stills)

moon_glow.about: issue 472: clouds crossing the moon, its pale light through their thin edges (stills)

moon_glow_late.about: issue 472: the moon lower in the small hours behind a thin edge (stills)

starlings.about: issue 380: a starling murmuration at dusk in November with nothing pinned: the seed picks how many, from which side, its passes, waves, streams and drops

starlings_beats.about: issue 380: a murmuration pinned short for stills of each beat: 220 in from the right with a stream behind, waves, two drops

gust_sweep.about: issue 380: a strong gust sweeps across the reeds and the trees, two smaller after it, a leaf torn off

shower_beats.about: issue 380: a passing shower at twelve times its speed (stills only): the cloud closing in from upwind, the gust front, the rain, the clearing, drips ringing the water and a rainbow with the sun behind you

van_shelter.about: issue 476: a morning shower at three times its speed (the shelter's own timing real): the rain sets in, he gets up and hurries to the van, in, the windows lit while it rains, then back to the log once it is over, with the rainbow

squirrel_oak.about: issue 343: a gray squirrel at true size against the oak: in along the shore strip in dashes and freezes, foraging, then up the trunk in bursts, out along the limb, a sit with tail flicks, and back down head first

hawk_perch.about: issue 330: the longer pass at a fixed seed: in from the left, the scatter, out past the right edge, back in a wide turn, a braking landing on the oak's main limb, a stay (cut short to 22 s for the clip) with a preen and a rouse, the heron frozen and no songbirds, then the crouch, the takeoff and away out the left edge

hawk_pass.about: issue 311: a songbird party and a pair down at the pond, a darner; the red-tail comes in, a few beats down, a low glide over the water, out; every bird bursts up into the far trees, the darner darts; silence, then they trickle back one or two at a time

bass_leap.about: issue 299: a darner low over the open water, the largemouth turning up under it, rising, breaking the surface, leaping (a miss, the darner jinks; then a catch), the splash and rings, a smaller second rise

turtle_log.about: issue 334: a painted turtle climbs out onto the log's far end and basks, at the size it swam at

fade.about: the open edges dissolving into the desktop (issue 424): bands along the world's left, right and bottom (points from its edge) when open (an open top is the sky's own dissolve), the lobes' wavelengths, reach and thinning width (fractions of the band), and where across a band the animals dissolve (life)

sound.about: The shell's sound engine (SceneSound, issue 413; proposal 2026-10-21-sound-in-packages): off by default; with the Sound switch on it reads the scene package's soundscape.json. The package sets each kind's loudness on the file (§3) and trims within -24..+3 dB; here the shell's own: master_db the whole mix, then a hard limiter at limiter_db (the proposal's -12 dBTP cap). fade_in_sec when it starts or the scene shows, fade_out_sec when it hides or turns off; event_attack_sec a one-shot's fade-in (nothing starts suddenly); bed_start_sec a weather bed coming in or going, bed_rotate_sec the handover to a slot's next clip at the end of a loop; silent_db below which a weather bed stops. voices per bus (the most a package may ask for). gust_share how much of SceneWind's gusts the wind bed adds to the mean. size_m the true lengths by_size spans (small .. large). callers_every_sec how often it looks for who is on screen to call; edge_margin_pt how far outside the scene an actor still counts as drawn (0: never). render: the off-screen render's presets (tools/sound_render.gd): a time, a weather, a seed, weather_speed, and clip events at seconds (SnapshotScene.event, plus weather: a phase to enter); crossfade_s squeezes the time beds' crossfade to keep pace with minutes_per_sec. The review minutes (issue 414): day_minute, dusk_minute, rain_minute.

pond_minute.about: A minute of the pond for the human's phone: a clear June morning, songbirds in, the heron hunting the shallows, the bass leap, turtles plopping off the snag; the wind gets up, a shower comes through and clears.

day_minute.about: A clear June day minute (issue 414): songbird parties singing a few times a minute, fish and turtles, the heron wading, geese landing, then a hawk pass that flushes the songbirds.

rain_minute.about: A minute of steady summer rain (issue 414): the rain bed over the ducked day bed, a few fish rising, the heron in the shallows, a song sparrow party sheltering.

dusk_minute.about: Dusk into night, sped up (a game minute a second, the beds crossfading over 15 s instead of 90 to keep pace): a robin and a cardinal singing at last light, then the dusk bed hands over to the night frogs and insects.

far_sky.about: the sky just beyond the far treeline, behind the far band's back plate and its trees: a starling murmuration at true size (issue 380), hidden by every tree it goes behind

far_sky_back.about: the far sky behind everything but the sky itself: a rainbow (issue 380)

mid_grass.about: behind the reed stand (mid z 2.5-2.69) on the right bank: an animal partly in the grass, coming out onto the shore strip or going in (issue 237); never for long (behaviour.grass)

water_back.about: fish toward the back of the cut-away: behind every weed (Skypatch issue 156)

water_front.about: fish near the glass: in front of every weed

mid_leaves.about: between the oak's trunk and its crowns: a bird perched among the leaves (Skypatch issue 134)
